With a massive NFL event comes numerous NFL betting opportunities for online sports betting . Fernando Mendoza is the overwhelming favorite to be selected No. 1 overall by the Las Vegas Raiders, but there are plenty of other DraftKings NFL Draft props than simply who gets selected first. Betting apps have plenty of 2026 NFL Draft props on individual players, positions and teams for prop betting on the NFL Draft. SportsLine NFL expert R.J. White has locked in some of his best bets for the 2026 NFL Draft at DraftKings, including picking star running back Jeremiyah Love, from Notre Dame, to be one of the first four picks in the NFL Draft 2026. White has locked in his five favorite DraftKings NFL Draft prop picks ahead of the opening round on April 23rd. Check them out below. NFL Draft predictions to target Ravens draft offensive lineman first (+130) The offensive line was a major issue for Baltimore last year, and it hasn't gotten any better with Tyler Linderbaum leaving for Las Vegas. Whether it's moving up a bit for Francis Mauigoa or Spencer Fano, taking a plug-and-play interior lineman like Olaivavega Ioane, or even selecting Kadyn Proctor as the heir apparent at left tackle, the Ravens should be using a draft like this that isn't considered stacked with blue-chip talent to stock up on help to address their biggest weakness. We saw a little shift from our initial recommendation to play this at +140 last week, but I believe it should be even odds at least. Trade NFL Draft props at Kalshi. Check out our Kalshi promo code review to see their latest offers. Carnell Tate draft position: Under 7.5 (-105) The market appears to be predicting a little bit of a slide for Tate after the Ohio State receiver was once considered the clear option for the Browns at No. 6. While I believe Cleveland will go with an offensive lineman at that spot, I don't know that Tate gets by the Commanders at No. 7, particularly if Jeremiyah Love and Sonny Styles go off the board in the top five. Tate would be a great running mate and eventual replacement for Terry McLaurin, and receiver is a clear need for Washington. Getting the underdog side of this market while having the potential to hit with either the Browns or Commanders seems like good value. Rueben Bain drafted before Mansoor Delane (-120) This is a head-to-head matchup available at DraftKings that I could see shifting quickly. Teams don't seem to be too worried about Bain's arm length, and on ability alone he has an argument to be taken in the top five in the same tier as Arvell Reese and David Bailey. Delane is probably the best corner prospect in the draft, though a team comfortable with Jermod McCoy's medicals could prefer him, and there is good enough depth at corner that I don't see Delane as a potential trade-up target like Bain could be. Bain's window could legitimately start at No. 4 overall and I can't see him getting past No. 9, while Delane's window starts at No. 8 and probably goes down to No. 12, unless the Cowboys are one of those McCoy teams. That leaves a small margin for Delane to win this matchup. Check out our bet365 bonus code review right now and get their latest sign-up promo. NFL Draft longshot picks Seahawks draft running back first (+380) The defending Super Bowl champions lost their Super Bowl MVP, and White thinks they may turn to the NFL Draft to replace him. The Seahawks declined to franchise tag or re-sign Kenneth Walker III after he rushed for 135 yards in Seattle's 29-13 Super Bowl win over the Patriots. Whether it's with the final pick in the first round or by trading back, White expects Seattle to prioritize a replacement. "No. 32 might be a little high for Jadarian Price, but I think there's a good chance the Seahawks are taking him with their first pick in a different spot," White said. "Running back is their clearest need with Kenneth Walker gone and Zach Charbonnet injured, and we saw how big an impact the rushing attack had in the Super Bowl last year. Seattle has just four picks and will likely prioritize adding more on Draft Day, and those late first-round picks are key for those looking to trade up (maybe for Ty Simpson?) as they come with a fifth-year option. I see the Seahawks making a trade back, then selecting Price in Round 2." Claim the latest BetMGM bonus code. Check out our BetMGM bonus code review now and get it. Jacob Rodriguez drafted in Round 1 (+380) With this draft class being perceived as short on top-tier talent, there is the potential for the back half of the first round to look even more different from consensus mock drafts than recent years. I see logic in examining the Round 1 pick market as a result for longshots we can take a chance on, and Rodriguez fits the bill. He and CJ Allen play a non-premium position at off-ball linebacker but have high floors and reasons to believe each could land in Round 1, especially to teams looking for a piece to come in and make an immediate impact. Rodriguez won a lot of hardware for his collegiate performance in 2025, and in particular, I could see a number of teams in the back half of Round 1 having him higher on their boards than we expect. Lions draft safety first (+3000) Brad Holmes is a best-player-available type of drafter, and with offensive lineman a massive -380 favorite in this prop, I see potential to take a big swing on a lottery ticket play. Detroit's pick at No. 17 is in the perfect range to target an excellent safety class that includes Dillon Thieneman (often tied to the Vikings one pick later) or Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, and even though the Lions have one of the best safety pairings in the league when healthy, there are injury concerns around both Kerby Joseph, who reportedly has a serious knee injury that clouds his long-term outlook, and Brian Branch, who tore his Achilles late last season. Every draft has position-team pairings in Round 1 that look surprising on the surface, and this is one that makes some sense. Looking to add some juice to the 2026 NFL Draft? An NFL player prop is a bet on how an individual player will perform in a game. Instead of betting on the winner, point spread, or total score, you're betting on a specific outcome or statistic for that player. Common NFL player props include: Passing yards, completions, attempts, and passing touchdowns (quarterbacks). Rushing yards and rushing attempts (running backs, quarterbacks, and other rushers). Receptions and receiving yards (wide receivers, tight ends, and running backs). Anytime, first, and multiple touchdown scorers (eligible offensive players and defenses/special teams). Most player props are offered as over/under bets. For example, a sportsbook might set a quarterback's passing yards at 245.5. You can bet the over if you think he'll finish with 246 or more, or the under if you think he'll finish with 245 or fewer. Touchdown scorer props work differently: you’re simply betting whether a player scores, with the odds reflecting the sportsbook's assessment of how likely that is. One thing that makes player props different from game bets is how much they depend on the game script. A team that falls behind by three scores is likely to throw more and run less, which can boost passing and receiving opportunities while cutting into rushing volume. That's why our projections account for the expected game script when estimating how a player is likely to perform. How Dimers finds the best NFL player props A prop is only worth betting if you have a number to compare the price against. Building that number is where most of the work happens. Market-specific model s: We model each of our prop markets separately, allowing the projections to account for the factors that matter most to each type of bet. Multiple models, combined : We use multiple models within each market and combine their predictions into a single projection. This helps produce a more robust estimate than relying on any one model alone. Player and game context : The projections consider player usage, recent and historical performance, injuries and availability, opponent strength, coaching tendencies, and the expected game environment. We also incorporate advanced metrics and play-by-play data. From projection to probability : We run simulations of the upcoming game to estimate how often a player finishes over or under the specific line being offered. That gives us the probability shown on the board. Probability meets price : We compare our projected probability with the probability implied by the sportsbook's odds. When our number is higher, the difference is the edge. Props that clear our value threshold make the board. Updated throughout the week : Projections change as player availability, team news, game conditions, and sportsbook prices change. Our board updates accordingly. Our NFL player props model is built to give you a consistent way to compare player projections with the prices available at sportsbooks. Rather than relying on a single prediction or a general opinion about a player, we use market-specific projections to identify where the numbers may offer value. NFL player props can change quickly as injuries, inactives, lineup news, game conditions, and sportsbook prices move. Our projections and board are updated throughout the week to reflect those changes. No model gets individual player performances right every time. Player props are inherently high-variance bets, and even a strong projection can lose on any given play or game. articles.text: Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions Skip to content Purchase Watch & Listen Login Dashboard Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions By Josh Shepardson | 2026-09-13T09:01:27-04:00 Sep 13, 2026 | View Larger Image NFL Best Prop Bets: Week 1 Picks Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Sharp Betting Tools: NFL Props: Lines & Odds NFL Spreads, Totals, & Moneylines NFL Weather Forecast & Potential Impact NFL Implied Team Totals NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Watson tore his ACL on January 5, 2025, in Week 18 of the 2024 season. He made his season debut last year on October 26, 2025, in Week 8. Remarkably, Watson didn't skip a beat. In fact, he played the best football of his career. The speedster can get off to a fast start this year, and the Packers might lean into the passing attack more while sorting through their backfield with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The matchup against the Vikings could also prompt them to pass more. Per TruMedia, the Vikings were tied for 12th in expected points added (EPA) allowed per designed rush in 2025 and fifth in yards before contact allowed per rush attempt (1.05). Minnesota's coverage tendencies also boost Watson's receiving outlook. According to the Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0, the Vikings were first in two-high coverage rate (69.0%) and first in blitz rate (44.7%) in 2025. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Kellen Moore brought his fast-paced brand of offense to the Saints last year. New Orleans played at the NFL's fastest pace in 2025, which is favorable for play volume. The Saints were only 19th in PROE (-0.6%), but their passing tendencies ratcheted up down the stretch. In the final four weeks of the regular season, New Orleans was tied for third in PROE (5.0%). They did play the Titans during those four weeks, and Tennessee's defense faced an NFL-high 6.4% PROE. However, the Saints also played the Panthers, Jets, and Falcons in that period, and they ranked 25th (-1.6%), 21st (-0.3%), and 20th (0.3%), respectively, in PROE faced in the 2025 regular season. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. Johnson can pick up where he left off for the Saints, and with New Orleans serving as one of the week's biggest underdogs, he should be in a negative gamescript, necessitating the Saints air it out to keep up with Detroit's high-powered offense. Winnipeg Blue Bombers vs. Edmonton Elks Winnipeg +4.5, -105 @ BetMGM Edmonton has been one of the CFL's biggest surprises this season, but this spread feels a bit too generous toward the home side. The Blue Bombers have had extra time to regroup following last week's victory over Ottawa and remain one of the league's most disciplined teams on both sides of the football. Winnipeg's defense has consistently limited explosive plays, which is critical against an Edmonton offense led by Cody Fajardo that thrives on sustaining long drives. For what it's worth, the Blue Bombers have allowed the fourth-most yards per game in 2026, and they'll be facing an Edmonton team that has generated the third-most yards on offense. Even if the Elks ultimately protect home field, Winnipeg has the experience and defensive playmakers to keep this game within one possession, not to mention an offense led by star-caliber players such as Zach Collaros and Brady Oliveira . Back the Blue Bombers to cover in this case. Hamilton Tiger-Cats vs. Toronto Argonauts Under 59.5 points, -105 @ FanDuel This matchup has all the ingredients of a shootout, but the total set at nearly 60 points simply looks too high here. Sure, Hamilton is coming off an emotional comeback victory over Saskatchewan, while Toronto returns home looking to bounce back after a lopsided defeat. And yes, both offenses possess enough firepower to move the ball consistently, and neither defense has been particularly reliable at preventing explosive plays throughout the season. The Roughriders remain one of the CFL's most complete teams when Trevor Harris is protected, and their balanced offensive attack prevents defenses from focusing on any one playmaker. While the Lions have shown flashes offensively, especially now that Nathan Rourke is back under center, the reality is that the team has struggled to consistently put together four-quarter performances, leaving the door open for Saskatchewan to capitalize. The Roughriders also possess one of the league's more physical defenses, a unit capable of generating pressure without excessive blitzing and forcing opponents into difficult second-and-long situations. While the Lions lead the CFL in yards allowed per game by a wide margin (339.6), it's hard to see their defense controlling the game against Saskatchewan's elite offense. Moore is coming off two lackluster seasons by his standards, but a new environment and the opportunity to play with Josh Allen may have created the perfect recipe for an excellent buy-low opportunity. Moore has been seen smiling throughout training camp as he enters 2026 in a dramatically different situation after being traded from Chicago to Buffalo. Instead of playing in an environment where something was clearly not right personally and in a Ben Johnson offense where his target share declined significantly, Moore now gets to catch passes from a former MVP quarterback while reuniting with Joe Brady , his former offensive coordinator in Carolina. The biggest reason to bet Moore’s over is simple: Allen is without a doubt the best quarterback Moore has ever had passing him the ball. Moore has spent most of his career dealing with inconsistent quarterback situations, yet he has still exceeded 1,000 receiving yards in four seasons. He enters his ninth season averaging more than 1,000 receiving yards per season. Moore is also a huge upgrade at the wide receiver position for Allen. The Bills have not produced a 1,000-yard-wide receiver in either of the previous two seasons since Stefon Diggs ’ departure, while their average target depth ranked last in the NFL in 2025. Moore doesn't need an unreasonable target share to beat his season-long receiving-yardage line, but he should command a target share over 20% given the receiver depth in Buffalo. The Bills entered the 2024 season with a new slogan: Everybody Eats. Sean McDermott tried to spin that into a positive after the Bills parted ways with Diggs. However, targets are earned. The “Everybody Eats” slogan was admitting to everyone what was glaringly obvious: There wasn’t an alpha target earner on the roster. In an interview, Ian Rapoport talked about Moore as a breakout candidate for the upcoming fantasy season, but fantasy gamers should be aware that “the Buffalo Bills like to spread the ball around.” Again, this is a mythical statement and is a byproduct of a lackluster receiving room. Diggs was a member of the Buffalo Bills from 2020 to 2023. In those four years, he led all NFL receivers in receptions, was second in targets, and had 28.0% of the Bills' total team targets over that span. Before last season, Moore had four consecutive seasons in which he had over 26% of his team’s targets. In 2021, Brady’s final season as the Carolina Panthers offensive coordinator, Moore had 28.3% of the team's targets and 40.2% of the team’s total air yards. In that season, Moore caught passes from Cam Newton , Sam Darnold , and PJ Walker and still exceeded 1,150 receiving yards. The projections in the Sharp Football Analysis Draft Kit are bullish on Moore joining the Bills. Our projections have Moore projected for 83 receptions and more than 1,100 receiving yards, well over the season-long yardage prop. One of the biggest risks of betting season-long overs is injury. Moore has played every game in the past five seasons and has played 15 or more games in all eight seasons to start his career. Moore has played through injury in the past, which helps give him the opportunity to continue to accumulate volume over the full season. The market may be overreacting to Moore’s 2025 season and overconfident that his decline is age-related. In addition to our projections supporting the over, in the Wide Receiver Trends article, Rich Hribar highlighted that when searching for wide receivers to exceed expectations, one of the more common hits comes from players changing situations, making Moore a solid bet this season. Given the way his role expanded throughout 2025, the 2026 season could be the year Loveland goes from promising rookie to legitimate NFL receiving weapon who is mentioned in the same sentence as Brock Bowers and Trey McBride when discussing the league’s high-upside tight ends. Since he joined the Steelers, Rodgers has seven interceptions in 17 games, for a rate of 0.41 per game, throwing just 14 turnover-worthy plays (TWPs) in that time, which equates to pretty neutral interception luck since just north of 50% of TWPs are picked. That jives with my model, as he has a -0.18 per-game "gift" average compared to league average, so when he throws defended passes, they are ones that are still difficult to be picked, showing his elite ball placement. His matchup against New England is solid too. Last year the Patriots had 10 picks in 17 regular season games. Yes, they had four against Stroud in a playoff game, but it was clear Stroud was totally rattled in cold conditions. Overall, the Patriots ranked as a slightly below-average defense in passes defended and interceptions, and so far in 2026 they haven't shown anything to make me think much differently. My Luck Rankings Dashboard is showing Rodgers with a projected 0.44 interceptions and just a 35.7% chance of having one. That means this is good to around -180, but to be safe, I'd play this to just -150. Pick: Aaron Rodgers Under 0.5 Interceptions (-135) Seahawks vs Cardinals Player Prop: Jeremiyah Love Rush Yards In his NFL debut, Love had 11 carries for 41 yards with a long of 18 yards. That means, outside of that carry, he averaged 2.3 yards per carry against the Chargers, who were an explosive play machine against opposing RBs last year, ranking 25th in stopping explosive runs to running backs. Now he faces a Seahawks defense that dominates on the ground, ranking first last year. Yes, they allowed Rhamondre Stevenson to hit a long of 12 yards, but it took him 18 attempts to do so. Love is a fantastic talent, but the attempts likely aren't going to be there, as he had 11 in a heavily leading game script in Week 1. Despite Drew Lock being at QB for the Seahawks, I think this will be a more neutral-to-Seahawks-leading script, and it's reflected in Love's rushing attempt line as books have him at 10.5 attempts, heavily juiced to the under. Yes, I know Ty Okada is out, and Nick Emmanwori is questionable, but they were the same status in Week 1 and Seattle shut down Rhamondre Stevenson on what projects to be around eight more carries than Love should have. I'd play this to -130 or so. Picks: Jeremiyah Love Longest Rush Under 11.5 Yards (-109 at DraftKings) Dolphins vs 49ers Player Prop: Christian McCaffrey Receiving Yards When the 49ers are 9.5-point favorites or more (within a half point of a field goal plus a touchdown), McCaffrey has an average of 37.5 receiving yards, but a median of just 30.5 in twelve games on 4.8 targets per game. In those twelve games, he cleared 40.5 yards just four times, but in each of those four he went for more than 65 yards. Trim that to 12.5-point favorites (within a half point of a touchdown plus two field goals) and he averages 35.9 yards with a median of just 27 on 4.0 targets across seven games. Miami got gashed by Ashton Jeanty last week, but that was in a game with no Brock Bowers in a game that was close partway through the third quarter. San Francisco has so many more weapons and projects to be in a bigger blowout that there's enough opportunity to spread the ball around here that McCaffrey's receiving volume probably isn't going to be massive. After all, as I mentioned above, he's averaged just four targets in heavily favored games. I'm projecting a median in the mid 30s, but there's always a chance CMC has a 70+ yard receiving game like he's done in two of the seven games he's played as a 49er as a super-heavy favorite. However, those were the only two heavily favored games he cleared 40.5 receiving yards as a 49er. Based on his splits, he's likely to stay under, but if he clears it, you could do worse than throwing a sprinkle on 60+ or 70+ alt receiving yards. Mandatory Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images CeeDee Lamb — Over 94.5 receptions Lamb has been one of the NFL's most productive and heavily targeted receivers when healthy, and I expect him to remain the centerpiece of Dallas' passing game. The key is volume, and 95 catches is a number Lamb can reach if he stays healthy. De'Von Achane — Under 1,000 rushing yards Achane is one of the most explosive players in football, but I'm betting against him reaching 1,000 rushing yards. His receiving ability gives Miami another way to utilize him, and I don't expect him to need a massive rushing workload to remain one of the Dolphins' most important offensive weapons. Jordan Mason — Over 4.5 rushing touchdowns Mason doesn't need to score 10 or 12 touchdowns for this bet to cash. I only need five. If he receives consistent opportunities near the goal line, I believe this number is very attainable. MORE: 4 NFL players with most pressure entering 2026-2027 season Kyren Williams — Under 9.5 rushing touchdowns NFL: NFC Championship Game-Los Angeles Rams at Seattle Seahawks Jan 25, 2026; Seattle, WA, USA; Los Angeles Rams running back Kyren Williams (23) runs to score a touchdown against the Seattle Seahawks during the first half in the 2026 NFC Championship Game at Lumen Field. Williams is obviously capable of scoring 10-plus touchdowns, but the Rams have enough offensive weapons that I don't want to assume he'll continue getting the same touchdown volume. I'm willing to bet he finishes with nine or fewer. Josh Allen — Over 24.5 passing touchdowns This number is simply too low for me. Allen threw 25 touchdown passes last season despite what was considered a relatively down passing year. One current market projection has him at exactly 24.5 passing touchdowns, while Sporting News also identifies the Over 24.5 as a strong 2026 prop. Caleb Williams — Over 3,645 passing yards I'm expecting Williams to take another step forward in Year 3. The current market projection is sitting at 3,649.5 yards, just above this number, which tells you how close this prop is. McBride is one of the best young pass-catching tight ends in the NFL, but asking him to catch 101 passes is a different proposition.
